topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and frames the study of the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamentals of the Complement System and C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core framework of complement by outlining its functional phases, clarifying its nomenclature, and describing the central biochemical role of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the three distinct recognition pathways initiate complement and converge to form surface-bound convertases.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes through which activated complement eliminates pathogens via opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the regulatory proteins that raise the activation threshold and prevent complement from damaging healthy host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical Presentations of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic analyzes the distinct pathological and clinical outcomes resulting from genetic or acquired deficiencies across the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the evolutionary strategies pathogens employ to circumvent complement-mediated immunity, focusing on the mechanisms of Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the session on complement and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
